title: TLR7/8 agonist design and delivery for effective anticancer immune response
text:
The studies proposed in this project will help advance an effective anticancer vaccine capable of providing
long-term protection against cancer. While the present studies focus on breast cancer, the novel agonists, materials
and techniques developed here will be broadly applicable to various cancer types.

title: Isolating hBCATm functions in human brain models
text:
Levels of the branched-chain amino transferase (BCAT) enzyme gradually increase in the blood vessels of
patients with Alzheimer’s disease as the disease progresses. This enzyme is important for breaking down
nutrients and supplying the brain with energy, but it is known to also have several ‘moonlighting’ support
roles. We will study the changes in brain nutrient and energy levels as the brain becomes stressed and BCAT
levels increase to learn about how BCAT supports the brain and how we might be able to help BCAT function
properly to treat the disease.

title: Countering microtubule stabilization within hair follicles in ovarian cancer chemotherapy
text: Alopecia is a major side effect of Taxol (paclitaxel), a key drug in the current treatment of ovarian and other cancers, used as a frontline agent in combination with carboplatin/cisplatin, and a second line drug with a dose intensive regimen following recurrence. We have made an important finding that low intensity ultrasound can effectively neutralize the cytotoxic effect of paclitaxel on cultured cells by disrupting paclitaxel-induced rigid and stabilized microtubule bundles, removing the cell killing activity of paclitaxel. The proposed study aims to develop and apply this discovery to protect the highly proliferative hair follicle cells from paclitaxel cytotoxicity, which will prevent short-term and permanent alopecia and improve the quality of life for cancer patients undergoing treatment

title: Cortical circuits for the integration of parallel short-latency auditory pathways
text:
Our brains generate a coherent perception of the sensory world by integrating information from parallel
sensory channels. This proposed study will delineate parallel auditory pathways that convey different
aspects of acoustic information in our brain and elucidate how they converge in the cerebral cortex to
generate unified sound representations. Our research will reveal neural circuit mechanisms underlying
auditory integration, the knowledge of which could point towards novel targeted treatments for hearing
disorders.

title: Patient-centered Development of a Composite Digital Endpoint of Mobility and Pain for Knee Osteoarthritis
text:
There is an urgent need to develop better treatments for chronic pain in people with knee osteoarthritis (OA).
One of the main challenges is that current methods don't always capture what matters most to patients or detect
changes in their pain and daily activities. This project will create a new way to measure how people with knee
OA walk and feel pain while walking, using sensors and a mobile app. This tool could help researchers find new
drugs and therapies that could improve the lives of millions of people with knee OA who struggle with pain and
difficulty moving.

title: Structure determination of amyloid oligomers and amyloid-TREM2 complexes
text:
Alzheimer’s Disease is a worsening public health crisis with no clear end in sight, and our
limited understanding of the molecular processes underlying the disease hampers our ability to design effective
therapeutic interventions. This study will investigate the so-far-unknown structures of amyloid oligomers and
amyloid-TREM2 complexes implicated in disease. Structures of these targets will enhance our understanding of
disease pathogenesis and identify new templates for structure-based drug design.

title: Digital Innovation, Simulation, and Collaboration using Virtual Environment Realities (DISCOVER) for Pediatric Diagnostic
text:
In this study, the DISCOVER (Digital Innovation, Simulation, and Collaboration using Virtual
Environment Realities) for Pediatric Diagnostic Excellence Learning Lab we will build a patient
safety learning lab combining the expertise of LiveWell, a design collaborative with user-centered
design and human factors expertise, with the clinical knowledge, implementation science
expertise, and world-renowned virtual simulation program of Cincinnati Children’s Hospital
Medical Center. This learning lab will use systems engineering methodology to envision, develop,
prototype and test design-informed clinical decision support approaches to improving diagnosis
in an existing highly immersive virtual clinical world.

title: A Program for Innovative PET Radioligand Development and Application - A Translational Toolbox for Treatments for Mental Health
text:
In this renewal application we propose to advance a unique, innovative program on the discovery,
development, validation, and application of novel radioligands for positron emission tomography imaging to
probe high priority molecular targets involved in mental health disorders. Success of this program will
contribute to the elucidation of the etiology and pathophysiology of mental diseases, and facilitate the
development of effective treatments.

title: Development of genetically encoded fluorescent reporters to detect a pediatric cancer biomarker in living cells
text:
Cancerous cells develop mechanisms to evade the checks and balances that control growth in normal cells,
including lengthening the caps, called telomeres, at the ends of chromosomes to promote cell division. Normal
cells do not use this mechanism, so disruption of telomere lengthening is a way to specifically target cancer cells.
We will develop a technology to follow in real-time, a telomere lengthening pathway that promotes cell division
in hard-to-treat pediatric cancers such as neuroblastoma, osteosarcoma, and glioblastoma.

title: Characterization of Lamprey B cells and Antibodies
text:
These studies in lampreys, a pivotal vertebrate representative, will yield insight into the basic evolutionary
principles of adaptive immune system development and function. The lamprey antibody producing cells will be
extensively characterized and their structurally unique antibodies with novel specificities engineered to exploit
their diagnostic potential in human cancers.

title: Studying stem cell-based therapies by applying advanced in vivo physiological and imaging methods to transplanted human neural populations in mice
text:
This proposal will develop new methods for studying the integration and function of hNPCs transplanted into
the mouse brain, thereby providing critical mechanistic insights that will advance the field of stem cell
transplantation as a therapy. Mice are one of the major mammalian model organisms for research on stem
cell transplant therapy and many organizational principles of cell types and circuits are conserved across
evolution, making them critical to understanding neurodegenerative and neurological disorders like Alzheimer’s
Disease, Parkinson’s and stroke. This proposal will establish new experimental paradigms to investigate the
cell and systems biology of stem-cell transplantation therapies and their functions, thus providing critical clues
into why some stem cell strategies are successful and others are not.

title: Unlocking Unstructured Data to Identify More Transplantable Lungs for the Right Recipients
text:
(i.e., public health relevance statement)
Nearly 4,000 lung failure patients are added to the national transplant waiting list each year, and while over
3,000 have their lives improved and extended by receiving a lung transplant, many die without a transplant.
Since only 20% of donated lungs are accepted for transplantation, opportunity exists to increase the number of
transplants and avoid waiting list deaths. However, because scientific evidence is lacking about which donated
lungs will have successful outcomes when transplanted into specific subgroups of patients (e.g., older or
younger, taller or shorter, emphysema or pulmonary fibrosis), our project will generate new evidence to assess
the quality of donated lungs and clinical decision support tools to predict whether a patient is expected to
survive longer by accepting a specific donor offer or waiting for a better transplant opportunity.

title: Automated Coding of Exposure Therapy Quality using Natural Language Processing
text:
This study will refine and test automated quality coding of exposure therapy, a highly effective treatment for
anxiety across the lifespan, using data from 6 existing clinical trials for youth and adults, across both research
and community settings. Specific aims are designed to validate automated coding with Natural Language
Processing (NLP; a type of artificial intelligence) against human coders, test predictive utility, and incorporate
stakeholder feedback to facilitate near-term usability of findings.

title: Elucidating Olfactory Epithelial Anti-Viral Responses in Persistent Post-Viral Olfactory Dysfunction
text:
Persistent smell loss after viral infections is common, especially in light of the COVID-19 pandemic, with
significant impacts on quality of life. This research will study the role of the innate immune system and how
local inflammation might cause hinder olfactory cell regeneration and cause persistent smell loss. A better
understanding of these mechanisms has the potential to guide development of novel therapies to treat post-
viral smell loss.

title: Decoding the molecular grammar of repressive condensates using spatial-functional screens
text:
Intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) organize nuclear architecture and regulate gene expression, yet we lack
a predictive understanding of how their sequence features encode condensate formation and transcriptional
repression. This project uses deep variant scanning, an IDR-focused protein language model, and high-
throughput imaging and transcriptional assays to define the sequence grammar of the HP1α IDRs in living cells.
The resulting rules will establish fundamental principles for how IDRs control chromatin organization and gene
regulation.

title: Structural Variation and Hematological Traits
text:
Blood cells are derived from bone marrow progenitor cells and released into circulation, where they play key
roles in oxygen transport, immune response, and blood clotting. In the proposed research, we assemble the
largest collection of participants with blood cell traits and whole genome sequencing and apply rigorous scientific
methods to interrogate genome-wide structural variation and functional characterization of the blood cell
associated structural variants. Results generated from this research may contribute to a better understanding of
blood cell biology and pave the way for new research into precision medicine for blood diseases.

title: Unraveling how Lipophilic Modulators Alter pLGIC Function via Interactions with the M4 Transmembrane Helix
text:
Responsible for fast synaptic transmission throughout the nervous system, pentameric ligand-gated ion channels
(pLGICs) are the targets of many drugs essential to the modern practice of anesthesiology and critical care
medicine, but drug development in this field has been stagnant for many years. In this proposal, I will use
advanced computational techniques to understand the structural determinants of pLGIC modulation via lipids,
which have been suggested to have molecular mechanisms that overlap with anesthetics. The outcome of this
work will be a detailed molecular model of how lipophilic species allosterically modulate pLGICs, opening new
avenues for drug discovery in anesthesia.

title: Effect of dietary restriction on intestinal stem cell aging
text: The integrity of the intestinal epithelium is essential to the overall health of the organism. With increasing age, intestinal integrity is compromised and is one of the factors that contributes to systemic inflammation and subsequently the deterioration of healthspan. The intestinal epithelium is highly dependent on the regenerative capacity of intestinal stem cells (ISCs) and interventions that improve intestinal function (and healthspan in general) are associated with increased activity of ISCs. Although the significance of ISCs is well recognized, the etiology of the age-related changes and the potential for specific interventions to reverse these changes remain unknown. Dietary restriction (DR) has been recognized as a key intervention that increases both health span and lifespan. In response to DR, increased activity of adult stem cells has been reliably reported in multiple tissues, including the intestine. We have published seminal data that brief periods of DR can induce substantial changes in gene expression within 1 month of its implementation. These changes persisted even after DR was discontinued suggesting induction of ‘cellular memory’. This application is designed to identify the epigenetic and transcriptomic mechanisms modified with age and re-activated by DR. Our long-term goal is to move epigenetic aging research from correlational analyses to mechanisms and develop the potential for therapeutic intervention. The overall hypothesis of this application is that age represses the expression of specific genes involved in ISC proliferation and differentiation by inducing changes in DNA methylation at specific genomic sites and these changes are reversed by short-term DR. We will measure both methylation (5mC) and demethylation (5hmC-hydroxymethylation) marks which functionally can regulate chromatin status and affect the ability of transcription factors and other DNA binding proteins to access DNA. This will be the first study to evaluate with high resolution the effect of DR on both 5mC and 5hmC levels with age. The aims are: Aim 1: Determine the specific window of intervention for optimal ISC function in response to DR. Aim 2: Identify DNA methylation changes induced by age and short-term DR in ISCs. Aim 3: Assess the effects of age and short- term DR on the ISC transcriptomes. Our longer-term goal is to reveal the specific mechanisms of DR in improving intestinal integrity and ISC function. After identifying specific genomic targets related to the actions of aging and DR in ISC, we will be in a position to use epigenome editing in ISCs using nuclease-deficient dCas9- fusion proteins tethered to enzymes involved in DNA methylation (e.g., Dnmts, Tets) at specific CG sites. Dr. Matlock Jeffries (previous Phase 1 CoBRE RPL) has agreed to assist us with this approach. These long-term goals will, for the first time, have the potential to identify the specific actions of DR on ISCs and have critical implications for aging and the effects of DR.

title: Causes and consequences of interpersonal microbial variation
text:
Humans carry enormous gut microbial communities that vary widely between individuals. The microbiome can
impact our response to diet and medical drugs. This research program aims to understand how gut microbes
modify these compounds and how interactions between gut bacteria determine microbiome composition and
function.

title: (Project 3) Extracellular Vesicles in Monitoring and Treatment of Dystrophinopathy
text: Principal Investigator: Nizar Saad Project Summary/Abstract Title: Extracellular Vesicles in Monitoring and Treatment of Dystrophinopathy. X-linked recessive Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is the most common muscular dystrophy affecting 1 in 3,500 boys. DMD is caused by mutations in the DMD gene, preventing the production of a fully functional dystrophin protein, which normally performs a critical structural role in stabilizing myofiber membranes during muscle contraction. Functional and clinical outcome measures for DMD were used in the clinical trial that led to the recent FDA-approval of the microdystrophin gene replacement therapy. The U7snRNA-based exon skipping is another promising one time single-dose gene therapy, aiming to restore full-length dystrophin expression, that entered clinical trial. The latter relies on similar outcome measures to validate therapeutic efficacy in treated patients. These outcome measures can be labor intensive, time consuming, inconvenient for some patients and expensive, which might delay approval of DMD therapies. Moreover, it is still unknown how efficacious these gene therapies would be in the larger DMD population and for how long their therapeutic benefits will last. Therefore, non-invasive, longitudinal monitoring of treated patients is needed to understand disease progression and assess persistence of therapeutic interventions and safer next-generation gene therapies with higher potency and possibility of re-administration are needed. In this project, we will rely on extracellular vesicles (EVs) to meet these needs. To identify novel circulating DMD and BMD biomarkers, we will investigate the RNA and protein content of circulating EVs collected from the plasma of DMD and BMD patients and healthy controls. EVs are lipid-bilayer delimited vesicles released by tissues or organs into biofluids and carry tissue/organ-specific molecules indicative of the pathophysiological state of their tissue or organ of origin. These molecules can be actively enriched in EVs. Therefore, their identification might allow the validation of EV-associated biomarkers that help track DMD and BMD onset and progression, stratify patients for trials, and serve as therapy responsive outcomes (Aim 1 and 2). AAV-mediated gene therapy for muscle diseases typically requires systemic delivery, which is challenging for first-generation AAV vectors due to high dose requirements for widespread muscle transduction. High dose, vascular AAV delivery has been linked to adverse events such as liver toxicity and AAV immunogenicity, which can reduce therapeutic efficacy and prevent administration to patients with pre- existing immunity to AAV. To overcome the challenges associated with systemic delivery of high AAV doses, we will package AAV with EVs. By enveloping AAVs with a lipid-bilayer, EVs may reduce total AAV capsid exposure, which would reduce the development of humoral immunity and shield AAV capsids from pre-existing anti-AAV antibodies. Previous work on EV-AAVs have demonstrated that enveloped AAVs were protected from anti-AAV neutralization. We will test the transduction efficiency and therapeutic potency of EV-AAVs in wild-type and DMD mice using as proof-of-concept AAV gene therapies investigated in Project 2 (Aim 3).
